title: Correlation Is Not Causation
paragraphs: Two things can happen together. This does not mean one causes the other.
Here is an example. In summer, people buy more ice cream. In summer, more people also swim. Sometimes swimmers are in danger in the water.
Ice cream does not cause this danger. The hot weather is the real reason. It makes people buy ice cream, and it makes people go to the water.
Scientists know this. They ask a simple question: is there a third thing? Then they test the idea with care.

questions.q: When do people buy more ice cream?
Does ice cream cause danger in the water?
What is the real reason in the example?
